title: Low copy number of the salivary amylase gene predisposes to obesity
authors: Falchi M, El-Sayed Moustafa JS, Takousis P, Pesce F, Bonnefond A, Andersson-Assarsson JC, et al.
population: Swedish obesity-discordant sibships, TwinsUK, DESIR and AOB15 samples of European origin; Singaporean Chinese replication sample
funder: Wellcome Trust (079534/z/06/z, 085555), Medical Research Council (K2010-55X-11285-13), Swedish Research Council, Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research, Swedish Diabetes Foundation, Swedish federal government (LUA/ALF) and European Community FP7 EUROCHIP; authors supported by the Medical Research Council, British Skin Foundation, Qatar Foundation, European Commission and Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust Biomedical Research Centre. The DESIR study was supported by INSERM contracts with CNAMTS, Lilly, Novartis Pharma and Sanofi-Aventis; by INSERM, Cohortes Santé TGIR, the Association Diabète Risque Vasculaire, the Fédération Française de Cardiologie, La Fondation de France, ALFEDIAM, ONIVINS, Ardix Medical, Bayer Diagnostics, Becton Dickinson, Cardionics, Merck Santé, Novo Nordisk, Pierre Fabre, Roche and Topcon.
result: In European samples, lower estimated AMY1 copy number was associated with increased risk of obesity (per-copy meta-analysis OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.13 to 1.26; P = 1.46 x 10^-10), corresponding to OR 7.67 (3.92 to 14.99) between subjects with more than 9 and fewer than 4 copies. Estimated AMY1 copy number ranged from 1 to 18.
